item.title: IEA to meet Wednesday over proposed release of oil, diesel stocks, two EU diplomats say
item.description: The International Energy Agency will hold an informal meeting on Wednesday to discuss a proposed release of oil and diesel stocks, two EU diplomats said, as details regarding the exact volume and ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: BRUSSELS -- The International Energy Agency will hold an informal meeting on Wednesday to discuss a proposed release of oil and diesel stocks, two EU diplomats said, as details regarding the exact volume and composition under the plan remained unclear. Record-high diesel prices have turned the fuel, which underpins trucking, agriculture and industry, into a global political and economic concern. The Group of 7 countries agreed last week to the new 100 million barrel release after U.S. President Donald Trump warned some European nations that the U.S. would ban diesel exports if they did not put more of the fuel into the market. The Paris-based IEA’s governing board was due to meet at 1300 local time (1100 GMT), the diplomats said. The G7 includes the U.S., U.K., Japan and Canada, along with European Union members France, Germany and Italy. The representatives of EU nations had already discussed the proposed release at a meeting on Wednesday morning, the diplomats added. Polish Energy Minister Milosz Motyka said on Wednesday that Poland was ready to release oil and diesel stocks if a consensus is reached, but he did not expect an IEA decision on this on Wednesday. The IEA’s board is expected to decide the details of the stocks release at an October 14-15 board meeting, two people close to the matter said on Tuesday. Extent of new volume not clear The IEA advises industrialized countries and coordinates their emergency oil stocks for use during major supply disruptions. In March, it agreed to release a record 400 million barrels of oil from strategic stockpiles to combat the spike in crude prices and supply losses that followed the start of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. Of this, about 325 million barrels have so far been released, the IEA said on Friday. It was not immediately clear on Wednesday if the G7 agreement would simply release the remaining share of the 400 million barrels, or add extra volumes on top of this, and how much would be diesel. Germany’s economy ministry said it was working on the approval of the release of energy reserves without mentioning any new amount. “Germany will participate in the further release of the volume already determined by the IEA in March,” the ministry said in a statement. As well as the war in Iran, the conflict in Ukraine has damaged oil refineries, helping to drive the rise in diesel prices. (Reporting by Kate Abnett and Holger Hansen; Additional reporting by Marek Strzelecki in Warsaw; Writing by Nina Chestney and Alex Lawler; Editing by Sudip Kar-Gupta, Jan Harvey and Joe Bavier)

item.title: Kenya infrastructure fund begins deploying $2.6 billion seed capital by buying bonds
item.description: Kenya's new National Infrastructure Fund has begun deploying its 340 billion shilling ($2.62 billion) seed capital by buying domestic government bonds, its chief executive said, in the first public disclosure of how it plans to finance projects.
item.dc:creator: Duncan Miriri
item.content:encoded: Kenya's new National Infrastructure Fund has begun deploying its 340 billion shilling ($2.62 billion) seed capital by buying domestic government bonds, its chief executive said, in the first public disclosure of how it plans to finance projects. President William Ruto announced the fund [USN:L5N3VN08R TEXT:"last October"] to finance infrastructure projects without placing additional strain on public finances. The fund's CEO James Mworia told Reuters that he expects the bond purchases to free up bank liquidity for private-sector lending. Commercial banks are among the largest holders of the more than $50 billion of outstanding domestic government securities, often preferring them to riskier private-sector lending. Burdened by high debt and annual repayments that consume 40% of government revenue, Ruto's administration has sought new ways to fund infrastructure. "We have a high debt service level relative to our income, we have high social needs and we have a limit to which you can tax Kenyans," Mworia said, explaining the rationale behind the creation of the fund. "But on the other hand, we have an infrastructure deficit." Kenya's domestic bond market is the government's main source of financing. Mworia said the fund began buying bonds in July, without saying how much has been invested. "It will give a liquidity boost to the rest of the market," Mworia said, arguing banks would likely lend more to businesses and households. INFRASTRUCTURE PLANS Mworia expects the fund to invest all its capital by the end of the financial year in June 2027. At 340 billion shillings, the planned investment is equivalent to roughly a third of Kenya's domestic borrowing target for the fiscal year ending June 2027, Mworia said. The bond portfolio is expected to generate about 42 billion shillings a year, helping the fund mobilise its targeted 3.6 trillion shillings over the next decade through co-investments and debt, Mworia said. The fund will invest in commercially viable projects in energy, transport and logistics, information and communications technology, water and farm sectors. The government capitalised the fund with proceeds from the [USN:L8N3ZS0PR TEXT:"privatisation"] of the Kenya Pipeline Company and the [USN:L8N3X927N TEXT:"sale"] of some of its shares in telecoms operator Safaricom. Through the fund, Kenya plans to take a stake in a [USN:L1N45M098 TEXT:"refinery"] under development by Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote in the coastal county of Lamu, Mworia said, without disclosing the size of the investment. The fund is also assessing other projects, he said. "We have a lot of interest from other investors who would like to co-invest alongside the National Infrastructure Fund," Mworia said, adding that co-investors will come from Kenya and abroad. ($1 = 129.8000 Kenyan shillings)

item.title: UK Conservative leader pledges to abolish inheritance tax on family homes
item.description: The leader of Britain's opposition Conservatives, Kemi Badenoch, pledged on Wednesday to abolish inheritance tax on family homes and let couples pass on an additional £1 million ($1.3 million) without incurring the levy if the party wins power.
item.dc:creator: Hannah McKay
item.content:encoded: The leader of Britain's opposition Conservatives, [USN:S8N3UD03A TEXT:"Kemi Badenoch"], pledged on Wednesday to abolish inheritance tax on family homes and let couples pass on an additional £1 million ($1.3 million) without incurring the levy if the party wins power. The Conservative Party, which has spent more time governing Britain than any other party, now sits third in opinion polls after [USN:L1N42U0AD TEXT:"years of political chaos"] and infighting in the aftermath of the [USN:L1N45M0A5 TEXT:"2016 vote to leave"] the European Union. On the final day of the Conservative Party conference, Badenoch put tax cuts and growing the economy at the heart of her speech, framing the next election as a "battle for the soul of this nation" and contrasting her economic vision with that of the [USN:L8N45L1RD TEXT:"governing Labour Party"]. Badenoch said she would like to abolish inheritance tax entirely when the British government can afford it, which is currently 40% of an estate's value over £325,000, or above £500,000 if a home is given to a direct descendant. "I believe the people who work hard and save should be rewarded for that effort," Badenoch said. BADENOCH SAYS WORK TO DO TO RESTORE TRUST Polling suggests a cut in or abolition of inheritance tax would be broadly popular. Inheritance tax is regularly named in polls as Britain's most disliked levy even though only about 5% of wealthy estates pay the levy. At its current level, the tax is expected to raise about £14.7 billion by 2030/2031, as rising property prices, particularly in London, mean a greater proportion of people are liable to pay it, according to research by the House of Commons. In the speech, Badenoch cast herself as a champion of lower taxes and government spending compared to the [USN:L8N43N0JB TEXT:"state-directed economic plans"] of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's Labour Party. Badenoch said Burnham's policies would make Britain "poorer" and accused him of wanting to spend "money we don’t have on things we can't afford". She also proposed to cut employer National Insurance social security contributions from the current rate of 15% to 7.5% for 21- to 24-year-olds to help them find work. Badenoch admitted there was "still a lot of work to do" to restore public trust in her party. "People are looking through the shop window, they like what they see, but not enough of them are buying yet," she said. "We need to fix that." ($1 = 0.7560 pounds)

DURBAN, Oct 7 : Australia opener Travis Head has taken to task former test players turned critics whom he accused on Wednesday of “putting a bullet” through the current team, who start the first test against South Africa in Durban on Friday. Head did not single out any pundit directly, but his strong remarks at a press conference came the day after Matthew Hayden, one-time holder of the record for the most runs in a test innings, accused selectors of “promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we've seen in a generation of cricket”.  The reference, made in a podcast, was about the recall of Nic Maddinson, who has been out of test cricket for nearly 10 years, but who joined the squad in South Africa after Josh Inglis fractured his finger and Cameron Green suffered a stomach injury. “I think it’s unfairly judged a fair bit from a group of past players, pretty much that put the bullet through a lot of players, which I think is unfair,” Head said.

“But that’s what they’re paid to do. Some of them need a job, so they go after us, and that’s totally fine. “This group is strong enough to deal with those sorts of things. That’s how it is. It’s unfortunate sometimes to have some of that feedback from a generation of players that we have huge respect for, but that’s the caper.” SELECTORS ACCUSED OF DISRESPECTING CRICKET Hayden accused the selectors of "disrespecting first-class cricket”, asserting that batsmen should have an average of 45 runs or more before being considered for test selection. But Head praised Maddinson’s abilities and the benefits of choosing experienced players for test cricket despite the 34-year-old replacement having a first-class average of 37.11. “We need mature guys that know what they need to be doing,” Head said. “And I think that revolves back to why we’ve been so good over a period of time, and why Australian cricket was so good back then in that era, because you’d bring in the Mike Husseys of the world, who are 30, who are tried and tested and know what they need to do.” Former Australia captain Allan Border suggested that the 32-year-old Head would face his toughest test as an opener against the South African bowling attack and would perhaps be better batting at number five.  “I have laughed at a fair bit of it because if a traditional opening batter had pushed out the same sort of numbers in his first 20 innings, I think he’d be pretty safe and not talked about in the way that it has been talked about,” Head said. "It’s a lot of headline stuff."

item.title: QatarEnergy's LNG expansion project poised to start operations in November, sources say
item.description: The first liquefied natural gas train under QatarEnergy's North Field East expansion project will be ready to start operation in November, two people aware of the company's plans said, offering Qatar a path to restoring some output lost to Iranian attacks.
item.dc:creator: Marwa Rashad
item.content:encoded: The first liquefied natural gas train under QatarEnergy's North Field East expansion project will be ready to start operation in November, two people aware of the company's plans said, offering Qatar a path to restoring some output lost to Iranian attacks. Launching the train would be a major milestone for the world's largest LNG expansion project at a time when Qatar is still recovering from the damage caused by attacks on Ras Laffan, which [USN:L6N407161 TEXT:"wiped out"] 17% of the country's LNG capacity. LNG production from the train is expected to start in the first quarter of 2027, the people said. QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. QatarEnergy Chief Executive Saad al-Kaabi [USN:L1N45D0BX TEXT:"said"] last month that the project was expected to begin production in the first half of 2027 despite the US-Israeli war against Iran and the resulting disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Mehdy Touil — lead LNG specialist at Calypso Commodities, which develops AI solutions for LNG — said the next major step will be the introduction of feed gas followed by a gradual progression over several weeks towards the first LNG production. "A sustained ramp-up will ultimately require the resumption of unrestricted transit through the Strait of Hormuz, but I expect QatarEnergy to have the first (North Field East) train ready regardless," he added. Iranian attacks in March on Qatar's Ras Laffan facility damaged two LNG trains, repairs to which could take three years to complete, and one gas-to-liquids plant that will complete repairs in the first quarter of 2027. Despite the damage, Qatar would be able to resume normal gas operations within weeks once the strait reopens, Kaabi said last month, adding that QatarEnergy is currently producing very little LNG.

item.title: Rahul Gandhi, Indian opposition lawmakers detained over election chief protest for second day
item.description: Indian police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"controversial revision"] of voter lists. Opposition parties, their student units, and the "cockroach" youth movement have been staging [USN:L1N45O03D TEXT:"almost daily demonstrations"] seeking Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation, after the Indian Express newspaper last month reported disagreements within the poll panel over updating voter lists, stoking concerns over its neutrality. Opposition lawmakers led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi [USN:L1N45S047 TEXT:"protested"] on Tuesday as well, seeking a meeting with Kumar and his deputies, before police broke up their gathering and briefly detained them. Wednesday's protest began after a lunch meeting of lawmakers that Congress organised at a restaurant in central Delhi, close to the Jantar Mantar site where authorities permit demonstrations. "Yesterday...Delhi Police stopped us and said you cannot protest here...so today...we will go to the designated protest site, sit there, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is not the legitimate commissioner," Gandhi told reporters, referring to Jantar Mantar. "The people who have done this (vote theft) are traitors...Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," he said, before boarding a bus that was to take the lawmakers to Jantar Mantar. NEW POLITICAL CHALLENGE TO MODI Lawmakers in the bus held posters against the windows that said, "no vote theft, no democracy theft", and "election commission, not BJP commission", referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. Hundreds of Congress members accompanied the bus on foot amid heavy deployment of police and paramilitary personnel in riot gear. Police also closed the road leading to Jantar Mantar, forcing the bus to take detour. Gandhi later stepped out of the bus, with a live feed on his party's YouTube channel showing him standing at the centre of a crowd of protesters and security personnel, while his sister Priyanka Vadra and other lawmakers sprawled out on the road. Visuals showed security personnel hauling Gandhi and Vadra into separate vehicles and taking them away. There was no immediate comment from the police on the detentions. The demonstrations present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, just months after similar protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) youth movement forced the [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"resignation of his education minister"] over exam paper leaks. Kumar has not commented on the voter lists issue but the election commission and BJP have denied accusations of wrongdoing.

LONDON, Oct 7 : Spanish Grand Prix organisers are planning to make changes to the Madring after complaints about the absence of overtaking and on-track thrills at this year's debut event, a spokeswoman for Formula One's newest circuit said on Wednesday. The grand prix hype ultimately turned into a procession that even some drivers said had risked sending them to sleep, despite the banked 'La Monumental' curve promising to deliver as a standout feature, after earlier fears of crashes and safety cars. Discussing the event at the Leaders Week London sports business conference at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge stadium, Juanco recognised there was work to do. "The complaints about the lack of action on track, that's something we're working on," she said.

"It's not a difficult thing to change, because it's just a small modification in certain corners, but as you know it's not in our hands. We need FIA approval, but we are working on it." Juanco said some pedestrian bridges would have to be moved after problems with visibility for some spectators sitting in certain grandstands. There were also gripes about the amount of time spent queuing for food and beverages in the fan zone. McLaren's reigning world champion Lando Norris, who lost a likely win after an early virtual safety car period, said after the race that the circuit needed to "get rid of" turns 18 and 19 and have more of a straight into the hairpin to allow overtaking. "I’m excited to come back here next year if they can make these changes because I think it’s a track that is good fun to drive and it can be a great racetrack. To me, it’s not a great racetrack," he added. Juanco felt the situation had been exacerbated by an excess of caution by teams and drivers after a spate of crashes in junior series races, both in testing and early in the race weekend, that triggered red flags and safety cars. There were also concerns about energy management with the new crop of hybrid cars, with engine tweaks already approved for next year.  "Finally, we had nothing, just a virtual safety car. And so I think we can improve the show on track next year where we are working on it," she said.

Oct 7 : Former Spain forward Pedro Rodriguez announced his retirement on Wednesday at the age of 39, bringing the curtain down on a glittering 20-year career that yielded 25 major trophies. Pedro, who became a free agent after leaving Lazio when his contract expired in July, was a key member of Spain's 2010 World Cup-winning squad and started in the final as they beat the Netherlands. He also helped Spain win Euro 2012. "I feel it is time. The time to take a step forward and begin a new chapter in my life," Pedro said in a statement on social media. "I leave proud of having lived my dream and of all the people who stood by my side to make it a reality. Thank you, football, for making me so happy."

He won the Premier League title in his second season at Stamford Bridge and later spent a season at AS Roma before crossing the city to join Lazio, where he spent the final five years of his career. Pedro made 794 appearances at club level, scoring 197 goals, while he netted 17 times in 65 appearances for Spain.

item.title: Tech companies tap debt, equity to fund AI and cloud expansion
item.description: The world’s largest technology companies are tapping debt markets and raising equity to bolster AI infrastructure, marking a shift for Silicon Valley firms that typically relied on cash to fund their ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: The world’s largest technology companies are tapping debt markets and raising equity to bolster AI infrastructure, marking a shift for Silicon Valley firms that typically relied on cash to fund their investments. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta signalled in April that spending on AI would not slow down. Tech giants’ combined spending is now set to exceed US$730 billion this year, up from about US$700 billion previously. The AI boom has entered a “more dangerous phase,” marked by exponentially rising investments in physical infrastructure and growing reliance on outside capital, according to an analysis by Bridgewater Associates in February. SpaceX SpaceX is looking to raise about US$10 billion in bank loans and US$30 billion in investment-grade debt to buy Nvidia chips, the Financial Times reported. Apollo Global Management is expected to lead the deal and help place the debt with a broad range of investors, with bond fund Pimco among a small group of lenders in talks to provide financing, the report said. CEO Elon Musk said during SpaceX’s August earnings call that the company would exclusively build on Nvidia going forward because “we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best.” Amazon Amazon.com is looking to raise at least US$25 billion from the U.S. bond market, Bloomberg News reported in July, citing people familiar with the matter. The tech giant filed for an eight-part offering of floating and fixed-rate notes, according to a regulatory filing. Amazon is issuing senior unsecured bonds, with maturities ranging from three to 40 years, as per a term sheet seen by Reuters. In June, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing that it has issued $14 billion of Canadian dollar-denominated notes, marking a record size for the Canadian corporate bond market. It is also preparing to issue a six-part bond offering in Swiss franc denomination for the first time, a person familiar with the matter had told Reuters in May. Separately, the e-commerce giant is looking to raise about US$37 billion in an 11-part bond sale, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters in March. Nvidia Nvidia in June said it would raise US$25 billion through a U.S. bond issuance, as it taps the debt market to increase liquidity for the first time since 2021. The bond consists of seven tranches of notes, maturing as late as 2056, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters. Salesforce Cloud software provider Salesforce in March said it has priced a US$25 billion debt offering to help fund a major share buyback. The company announced a US$50 billion repurchase program and lifted its dividend by 5.8 per cent in February. The company had last issued U.S. bonds in 2021, securing US$8 billion to support its acquisition of communication platform Slack. Oracle Oracle in February said it expects to raise US$45 billion to US$50 billion in 2026 in a combination of debt and stock to build additional capacity for its cloud infrastructure. The cloud company was sued in January by bondholders who said they suffered losses because the company failed to disclose it needed to sell significant additional debt to build out its AI infrastructure. In September 2025, the company, chaired by Larry Ellison, filed to raise about US$18 billion in debt in a six-part offering to fund AI infrastructure, after investing billions in 2025. Alphabet Alphabet is looking to raise between US$20 billion and US$25 billion from its latest U.S. bond offering, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. The company is offering notes in as many as 10 parts, a regulatory filing showed. The offering comes two weeks after the Google parent raised its 2026 spending forecast and highlighted plans for increased AI-related investments amid growing investor scrutiny of returns on such spending. In June, the company said it was looking to raise US$80 billion in equity offerings, including an investment from Berkshire Hathaway. It increased the size of its equity offerings to US$84.75 billion after seeing strong investor demand. The deal brings in Warren Buffett’s diversified holding company as a major new investor, adding a high-profile endorsement of Alphabet’s long-term AI and cloud strategy. Alphabet also plans to sell Japanese yen-denominated bonds for the first time, it disclosed in a filing in May. The issuance is expected to total several hundred billion yen, a source with direct knowledge of the deal said. The tech giant sold a rare, 100-year bond worth 1 billion pounds (US$1.35 billion) in February, as part of a global US$31.51 billion debt raise. The company sold 5.5 billion pounds worth of sterling bonds in a five-part deal, according to the final term sheet seen by Reuters. It had in November last year filed to raise US$17.50 billion in debt in the U.S. and 6.5 billion euros (US$7.50 billion) in Europe, for general corporate purposes, including the payment of outstanding debt. Verizon The U.S. carrier had in November last year filed to raise about US$11 billion in the corporate bond market to help fund its US$20 billion acquisition of fiber-optic internet provider Frontier Communications, which it closed in January. Meta platforms The Facebook owner had in October last year filed for its largest bond offering ever, of up to US$30 billion, to finance a costly AI infrastructure expansion. Meta has been navigating significant cost pressures from AI investments, boosting its capital spending plans by 73 per cent this year to offer personalized AI to its large social media user base. SOURCE: Data compiled by LSEG; SEC filings (Reporting by Anhata Rooprai, Zaheer Kachwala, Johann M Cherian, Harshita Mary Varghese and Prathik Jayaprakash in Bengaluru; Editing by Leroy Leo, Arun Koyyur, Anil D’Silva, Sahal Muhammed, Shilpi Majumdar and Jonathan Ananda)

item.title: Lower US Treasury yield view persists despite biggest quarterly surge since 1994: Reuters poll
item.description: US Treasury yields are forecast to fall over coming months, according to fixed income strategists in a Reuters poll who clung to their long-held view despite the benchmark 10-year yield recording its biggest quarterly jump since 1994.
item.dc:creator: Sarupya Ganguly
item.content:encoded: US Treasury yields are forecast to fall over coming months, according to fixed income strategists in a Reuters poll who clung to their long-held view despite the benchmark 10-year yield recording its biggest quarterly jump since 1994. However, conviction behind calls for lower yields, which strategists have been [USN:L6N4520Y7 TEXT:"consistently wrong"] about over the past nine months, appears to be wavering. Some strategists are basing their views on the position that financial markets have overdone pricing in a series of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and policymakers may end up doing less. Meanwhile, government borrowing costs have hit [USN:L1N45N082 TEXT:"multi-decade peaks"] in many developed economies in recent weeks on fears of inflation from the US-Israeli war with Iran and rising central bank policy rates. [USN:L6N45N0Q6 TEXT:"Heavy borrowing"] by tech giants to fund the AI buildout, coinciding with increased Treasury issuance, is only adding to rising yield pressure. FED OUTLOOK GUIDING YIELD VIEW Median views from nearly 60 strategists polled October 5-7 showed the benchmark yield easing around 30 basis points to 5.00% by year-end, 4.90% in six months and 4.75% in a year. The 10-year yield has risen almost 120 basis points this year and is trading a whisker away from the 5.34% it hit last week, the [USN:L8N45N0EQ TEXT:"highest since 2002"]. "Unless the Federal Reserve hikes a lot more aggressively than we expect, yields are probably a little too high," said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research. He said his models pointed to yields being more fairly valued between 4.50% and 5.00%. Interest rate futures are pricing in at least three more Fed rate rises over the coming months. The latest set of Fed [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"policymaker forecasts"] implied at least one more was coming this year. That speculation has pushed up the rate-sensitive two-year yield roughly 40 basis points in the last month. According to the poll, it was forecast to fall about 10 basis points to 4.70% in three months, 4.60% in six and 4.25% in a year. Still, all but 2 of a subset of 30 forecasters answering an additional question in the survey said the 10-year yield was more likely to land above their forecasts rather than below in the near term. NINE MONTHS OF MISSES The recent US Treasury yield surge comes despite efforts from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in August to alter the schedule of debt issuance and attempt to increase long-end [USN:L1N44H0P5 TEXT:"buybacks"]. Reuters poll data show strategists have underestimated the 10-year yield's rise in nine straight monthly surveys this year, getting the direction mostly wrong in six of the most recent months. Unexpected resilience in US growth is one reason. US GDP rose at a far-above-consensus [USN:L1N45L0XU TEXT:"2.2% annualised rate"] in the second quarter. Foreign exchange strategists have also had a [USN:L6N45O04G TEXT:"bad run"], calling for dollar weakness on the 6-12 month horizon for at least half a decade and getting it wrong as a group most of the time over the last two years of monthly FX polls. Three- and 6-month forecast ranges for the 10-year yield were also the widest since March. Nordea, among the earliest in the surveys to correctly call higher yields, did so on the "stickiness of inflation pressures in the US", its chief analyst Jan von Gerich said. There was "a straightforward case" that term premium, the additional compensation investors demand for holding longer-dated debt, "has been too low", he added. Rates have entered "a different regime" from anything seen since the global financial crisis, said Meghan Swiber, director of US rates strategy at Bank of America. "Long-end rates are really telling the Fed they should be doing more to tighten and rein in financial conditions — and a Fed not doing that is going to pay the consequence through higher longer-term rates," BofA's Swiber added. "This is a divergence from how investors have been looking at rates over the past several decades. And there is inertia in investors' thinking about how high rates are going to go."

item.title: Francia suspende el uso de granadas aturdidoras para controlar las protestas estudiantiles
item.description: El Gobierno francés anunció el miércoles que suspenderá de forma temporal el uso de granadas aturdidoras en su actuación policial ante las protestas estudiantiles, después de que un joven de 15 años perdiera una mano durante un enfrentamiento con la policía antidisturbios.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Delame, Makini Brice
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno francés anunció el miércoles que suspenderá de forma temporal el uso de granadas aturdidoras en su actuación policial ante las protestas estudiantiles, después de que un joven de 15 años perdiera una mano durante un enfrentamiento con la policía antidisturbios. Organizaciones de derechos humanos, estudiantes y algunos opositores políticos han acusado a la policía francesa de emplear una fuerza desproporcionada durante una ola de protestas estudiantiles que dura ya más de dos semanas y que ha puesto de manifiesto un profundo descontento social de cara a las elecciones del próximo año. El ministro del Interior, Laurent Núñez, dijo que ordenó la suspensión del uso de granadas aturdidoras hasta que se aclaren los hechos ocurridos el lunes en la ciudad norteña de Lens. Asimismo, indicó que hay una "gran probabilidad" de que el disparo de una granada aturdidora no letal hubiera provocado la pérdida de la mano del joven. "Suspendo su uso en el marco del movimiento de los estudiantes de secundaria hasta que se aclare lo ocurrido en este caso", declaró el ministro, quien añadió que se habían remitido un total de 18 investigaciones a la inspección de policía. Los estudiantes de secundaria están indignados por el mal estado de las infraestructuras, la falta de profesores, los horarios sobrecargados y la falta de financiación en educación. Atribuyen el empeoramiento de los resultados de Francia en el Programa para la Evaluación Internacional de Alumnos (PISA) de la OCDE a las malas condiciones de aprendizaje. Según las clasificaciones, estos resultados han caído más rápidamente que la media de la OCDE desde 2015. Las protestas no daban señales de amainar el miércoles, con más de 500 centros educativos cerrados un día después de que las manifestaciones se extendieran por todo el país. Los sindicatos convocaron otra jornada de marchas callejeras para más adelante esta semana. El primer ministro francés, Sébastien Lecornu, ha reconocido las reivindicaciones "legítimas" de los estudiantes franceses, pero también ha calificado los disturbios como las manifestaciones estudiantiles más violentas de las últimas décadas.

FAST

LONDON, Oct 7 : Manchester City should own up to their breaches of the Premier League's financial rules and accept their punishment, former England captain Gary Lineker said on Wednesday, adding he would not be surprised if they were ultimately stripped of titles. City were found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the league's financial rules over nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as three out of four charges concerning failures to cooperate with the investigation. The league said that City had used "sham" commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million ($1.19 billion) over nearly a decade, during which time they won multiple trophies. City have appealed the ruling and insist they are innocent. Former Everton, Tottenham Hotspur and Barcelona forward Lineker said the whole debacle was damaging for the club and the English game, but that City admitting their guilt would go some way to draw a line under the saga.

"Obviously it looks really bad for Manchester City, it really does. And bad for the game... I'd love to see Man City now just own it and just say, 'OK, we got it wrong'," Lineker told reporters at the Leaders Week sports industry conference at Stamford Bridge. "'But for the good of the game, we'll accept it, we'll accept whatever punishment comes our way and we'll carry on'. I think that would be a blessing and save their face a little bit at the moment, though that doesn't look very likely," he added. "But it is damaging... and I feel for their fans and I feel for their players."  Asked if City should be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won in the disputed period, Lineker said: "I wouldn't be surprised if it goes down that route. But again, ultimately, who suffers from that? The players and the fans." The appeal will take place in private. It remains unclear whether sanctions will be announced before the appeal is heard, and whether they would take effect immediately. City top the Premier League standings on 15 points from five games and seek a sixth straight win at Liverpool on Sunday.  .

Source: Reuters

item.title: Titan Mining signs preliminary deal with U.S. Army for Alabama graphite facility
item.description: Titan Mining said on Wednesday its subsidiary signed a preliminary agreement with the U.S. Department of the Army outlining commercial terms for a proposed graphite processing facility in Alabama.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: Titan Mining said on Wednesday its subsidiary signed a preliminary agreement with the U.S. Department of the Army outlining commercial terms for a proposed graphite processing facility in Alabama. The agreement comes as the United States moves to expand domestic processing capacity for critical minerals used in defense, battery and industrial applications. Here are more details: The proposed facility would be developed on about 97 acres of underutilized Army property at Anniston Army Depot in the state. Under the term sheet, Titan’s unit Empire State Mines would develop, finance, build, own and operate the graphite processing facility. The Canadian company said the facility would produce Purified Micronized Graphite — used in industrial, defence and battery applications — and later Coated Spherical Purified Graphite, a key material in lithium-ion battery anodes. The proposed lease framework includes an initial 50-year term with two 25-year renewal options, providing potential operating tenure of up to 100 years. The Army would have a right of first offer on certain uncommitted PMG and CSPG output, capped at 10 per cent of annual facility production. (Reporting by Varun Sahay in Bengaluru; Editing by Vijay Kishore)

item.title: India's Jubilant FoodWorks posts higher quarterly revenue as Domino's sales pick up
item.description: India's Jubilant FoodWorks said on Wednesday its consolidated revenue for the second quarter rose 11.9% on-year, driven by healthy sales at its Domino's pizza outlets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Jubilant FoodWorks (JUBI.NS) said on Wednesday its consolidated revenue for the second quarter rose 11.9% on-year, driven by healthy sales at its Domino's pizza outlets. Quick-service restaurant operators are seeing demand recover after a sluggish start to the year. Motilal Oswal analysts expect growth to accelerate in the second quarter from the previous three months, although elevated fuel and raw material costs continue to weigh on margins. The company, which operates Domino's Pizza (DPZ.O) outlets in India, reported a consolidated revenue of 26.09 billion rupees ($269.89 million) for the three months ended September 30, it said in a pre-earnings quarterly update. Standalone revenue rose 11.6% to 18.86 billion rupees. Domino's India recorded like-for-like growth of 4.1% during the quarter, up from 2.5% in the June quarter. Jubilant did not provide like-for-like sales figures for its other brands. In August, the company said its fried chicken brand Popeyes was emerging as a second growth engine, while efforts to revive dine-in and takeaway sales at Domino's, which have lagged its stronger delivery business, were showing signs of success. Jubilant said it added a net 108 stores across its brands during the quarter, taking the total group network to 3,820 stores as of September 30. ($1 = 96.7750 Indian rupees)

item.title: Funcionario iraní dice que pronto se bloquearán "rutas ilegales" del estrecho de Ormuz
item.description: Las rutas de tránsito en el estrecho de Ormuz que Irán considera ilegales se cerrarán en breve, dijo el miércoles un asesor del comandante de la Guardia Revolucionaria (CGRI) a la agencia de noticias semioficial Fars, refiriéndose a la ruta sur que bordea la costa de Omán.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las rutas de tránsito en el estrecho de Ormuz que Irán considera ilegales se cerrarán en breve, dijo el miércoles un asesor del comandante de la Guardia Revolucionaria (CGRI) a la agencia de noticias semioficial Fars, refiriéndose a la ruta sur que bordea la costa de Omán. Mohammadreza Naqdi dijo que estas "pocas rutas" se crearon mediante voladuras y dañando algunos de los pasos rocosos de esta vía navegable estratégica, y que eran utilizadas por "pequeñas embarcaciones que contrabandeaban petróleo y lo transferían a petroleros". Esto contradice la narrativa de que las exportaciones de petróleo del golfo Pérsico están recuperando los niveles previos a la guerra. "El estrecho de Ormuz está cerrado y las fuerzas armadas de la República Islámica de Irán tienen pleno control sobre él. Esta situación se mantendrá hasta que se satisfagan las demandas legítimas de Irán", añadió. El promedio móvil de siete días de las exportaciones de crudo de la región fue de 18,3 millones de barriles al 30 de septiembre, según datos provisionales de Kpler, y los volúmenes superaron los niveles previos a la guerra durante 14 días en septiembre. Esto incluía el petróleo del golfo Pérsico enviado a través de Ormuz, el mar Rojo y desde terminales y trasvases de barco a barco en el golfo de Omán. El CGRI ha negado de manera sistemática que los flujos de crudo en el estrecho se estén recuperando gracias a la ayuda de la Armada de Estados Unidos, y otro asesor del CGRI, Majid Mirahmadi, dijo el jueves que por la vía transitan un promedio diario de 10 buques, frente a los 125 de antes de la guerra que comenzó el 28 de febrero, cuando Estados Unidos e Israel mataron al líder supremo, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei, en un ataque aéreo en Teherán. A pesar del aumento de los flujos de petróleo en septiembre, los ataques iraníes contra petroleros y las limitaciones logísticas han persistido y ponen en duda que el aumento de los flujos pueda mantenerse de forma permanente.

item.title: Gauff falls to Mertens at China Open after 'draining' few days
item.description: Coco Gauff crashed out of the China Open in the last 16 on Wednesday, suffering a 6-3 6-3 defeat by Belgium's Elise Mertens in what the American third seed described as a "draining" few days.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Coco Gauff crashed out of the China Open in the last 16 on Wednesday, suffering a 6-3 6-3 defeat by Belgium's Elise Mertens in what the American third seed described as a "draining" few days. Gauff revealed after her victory over Chinese 16-year-old Sun Xinran on Monday that she had received an [USN:L4N45S06O TEXT:""insane" amount of racial abuse"] on social media following a match in which a replayed point sparked an online backlash. Asked what the previous 36 hours had been like, the 22-year-old told a news conference: "It has been kind of draining, I'm not going to lie. I just turn off my phone and move on. There's nothing you can do." Gauff beat Sun 7-5 6-1 to reach the fourth round, but was targeted online after stopping play during a key point in the first set, raising her hand to complain about a flickering advertising board just as Sun was about to put away a winner. After a video review, the umpire ordered the point to be replayed. Gauff won the replayed point and held serve for 5-5 before going on to seal victory over Sun. Gauff later said she had received a barrage of abusive messages on social media after the match. The WTA condemned the abuse. "There is no place for racism, discrimination, or abuse in tennis," the WTA told Reuters in a statement. "We are appalled by the racial abuse directed at Coco Gauff and are in contact with her to offer our full support. "As we do for all WTA players experiencing online abuse, our Threat Matrix team is monitoring the abusive messages, working with the athlete's team to report them to the relevant platforms and seeking action on the content and the accounts responsible." The Threat Matrix service was launched in 2024 and uses AI and open-source data to help protect athletes from online abuse and harassment. The defeat against Mertens capped a difficult few days for the two-times Grand Slam champion, who had beaten the 30-year-old Mertens in all five of their previous meetings. The 13th seed reached her first Beijing quarter-final in her seventh appearance at the WTA 1000 tournament and will next face six-times Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek. "My coach/boyfriend (Christopher Heyman), it's his birthday tomorrow," Mertens said in her on-court interview. "So for me, this win is dedicated to him." Gauff's challenge unravelled amid a barrage of errors, with the 2024 Beijing champion committing 34 unforced errors, including eight double faults, during the 78-minute defeat. Gauff struggled to find her rhythm throughout the contest and, trailing 4-1 in the second set, told her team courtside that she had "no energy" and felt as though she might pass out. "I think I just didn't play well," Gauff said. "I think I wasn't moving well. There were a lot of things I didn't do well. I thought Elise played well on the big points, made me play a big ball, yeah."

FAST

Oct 7 : Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, who last season guided the club to their first Premier League title in 22 years, has signed a new contract until June 2030, the English champions announced on Wednesday. Arteta, who took charge at a time of crisis in 2019, has been at the heart of a long-term turnaround plan that has restored the club's status as one of the best teams in Europe. “It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal," Arteta said in a statement. "This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue."

Arteta ended his playing career in 2016 after five years at Arsenal, and joined Pep Guardiola's backroom staff at Manchester City as an assistant coach. But he returned to Arsenal three years later, taking over from Unai Emery with the club struggling in 10th place in the Premier League. Under the Spaniard, Arsenal returned to the league's top-five in 2021-22, and finished second three times straight before finally being crowned champions last season. They also reached the Champions League final, where they lost to Paris St Germain in penalties. “This is an important time in Arsenal Football Club’s history. We want to create a winning era together with Mikel," club CEO Richard Garlick said. The club management backed Arteta's plan to rebuild the team, reinforcing the defence and midfield with signings like Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard and Ben White, and goalkeeper David Raya. The investment paid off, with Arteta delivering a 62.05 per cent win-percentage after 361 games in charge, the best among all full-time Arsenal managers. “We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together," the 44-year-old Arteta added. Arsenal, second in the league, will return from the international break with a home game against Leeds United on Saturday.

item.title: US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest in nearly three years
item.description: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to to 7.49%, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if the Republicans keep control of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump's Republicans keep control of Congress. The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage surged 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. It was last higher in November 2023. Mortgage rates are tied closely to the yield on US 10-year Treasury notes, which earlier this week hit a 24-year high, driven by worries over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth. The cost of living is the top issue on Americans' minds as they decide how they will vote on November 3, a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday showed, and is one reason why Trump's [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"approval rating"] is at a record low of 32%. Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, which topped 5.3% on Monday. Inflation is also on the rise, registering 3.4% in August by a measure that the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. Fed policymakers have signaled they expect to follow their September interest-rate increase with another rate hike by year's end, though markets are for now betting they will not move at their upcoming policy meeting at the end of October. Mortgage loan applications fell 4.2% last week from the previous week, the MBA said on Wednesday, with refinancing applications dropping sharply. Overall application volumes are the lowest since February 2025 and have fallen nearly 50% since January. "Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," said Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist.

item.title: ロシア当局「ペスト流行リスクなし」、研究職員死亡巡りメディア批判
item.description:
Andrew Osborn Jennifer Rigby
［モスクワ／ロンドン ７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Osborn　Jennifer Rigby

［モスクワ／ロンドン　７日　ロイター］ - ロシアの衛生当局は７日、東部シベリアのペスト研究所の職員が死亡した事例について、同地域で流行が広がるリスクはないと表明した。一方、世界保健機関（ＷＨＯ）はロシア政府に対し、死因に関するさらなる情報の提供を求めている。

シベリア地方のイルクーツク州にある研究所の女性職員（２８）が２日、原因不明の肺炎で死亡した。この事例を巡っては、トランプ米大統領を含め国際的な懸念が広がり、当初は約２００人が隔離対象となった。

ロシアの衛生監視機関である消費者権利保護・福祉監督庁（ロスポトレブナゾール）は声明で、流行のリスクはないと結論付けたとして予防措置を縮小しつつあると表明。ＷＨＯとも最新情報を共有したとした。死亡した職員と接触した人の中からペストの症例は確認されておらず、約５０００件の検査でも危険な病原体は検出されなかったため、隔離対象者の９０％が解除されたという。

また、同職員はワクチン接種を受けており、「業務で扱っていた危険な感染症に対する免疫を獲得していた」とした。ただし、死因となった肺炎の原因や感染経路については明らかにしなかった。

＜大統領府、メディアの「虚偽情報」を批判＞

ロシア大統領府のペスコフ報道官は、所定の手続きに従って事件についてＷＨＯに適切に報告したと述べた。メディア報道を事態の根拠として用いることに慎重であるべきだとした上で、「報道は非常に多いが、メディアがこの件について伝えていることの大半は虚偽の情報だ」と批判した。

ペスコフ氏はメディアなどに対し、衛生当局の発表する情報に依拠するよう助言した。

米ＡＢＣニュースはこれに先立ち、「米国がこの死亡事例へのロシアの対応について正式な外交抗議を申し入れ、ロシアに対し同事例に関する透明性の向上を求めた」と報じていた。

ペスコフ氏はまた、現時点ではプーチン大統領とトランプ米大統領との間で電話会談の予定は入っていないと述べた。トランプ氏は６日、この件について「まもなく」プーチン氏と話し合うと述べていた。

item.title: South Korea denies Ukrainian report that it eased Russia's fuel crisis
item.description: South Korea's presidential office on Wednesday dismissed a Ukrainian report that Russia has imported petroleum products from South Korean ports, calling the accusation inappropriate.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's presidential office on Wednesday dismissed a [USN:L8N45S1BB TEXT:"Ukrainian report"] that Russia has imported petroleum products from South Korean ports, calling the accusation inappropriate. Ukraine's top sanctions official, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, said on Tuesday the shipments had eased the impact of a fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. His comment followed a report by the Guardian newspaper saying that port records and ship-tracking data showed that fuel had been loaded at South Korean ports onto seven tankers, including vessels under British and EU sanctions. The presidential office said South Korea had "consistently enforced sanctions and export controls against Russia in close coordination with the international community," since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine . It added that Seoul was examining the facts and checking for any export control issues, and would take necessary measures if any problems were confirmed.

item.title: 独、テスラの運転支援システムのＥＵ承認を推進 マスク氏が歓迎
item.description:
Marie Mannes Miranda Murray
[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テス...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独、テスラの運転支援システムのＥＵ承認を推進　マスク氏が歓迎 19:43 配信

資料写真：2026年4月14日、中国・上海で行われた政府主催のメディアツアーの際に、テスラ・ギガファクトリーに掲げられたテスラのロゴ。 REUTERS/Go Nakamura/File Photo

Marie Mannes　Miranda Murray

[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は７日、同社の運転支援システム「フルセルフドライビング」に対するドイツ政府の支持を歓迎した。同氏は、交通安全の専門家らが「安全性の主張が誇張されている」と警告する「フルセルフドライビング」について、欧州全域での承認を目指している。

マスク氏は、ドイツのビルガー交通相が欧州全域での「フルセルフドライビング」の承認を推進していることを受け、Ｘにドイツ語で「ありがとう」と投稿した。

ビルガー氏は６日の声明で、先月にテスラと数多くの技術的詳細や責任問題について協議した結果、「フルセルフドライビング」のＥＵによる迅速な承認を提唱していると述べた。

協議の一環で、ドイツはテスラと、「フルセルフドライビング」で制限速度を最大１０％まで超過してもよいことで合意した。速度超過が主な争点の一つとなっている欧州の承認プロセスにおいても、ドイツはこのアプローチを支持する方針だ。

一方、交通安全の専門家や一部の規制当局は、テスラが採用している「速度オフセット機能」（システムが制限速度を超えて走行することを可能にする機能）は、欧州での承認前に削除されるべきだと主張している。

ビルガー氏はまた、システム名が多少誤解を招くという懸念に対処するため、テスラがシステム名を「テスラ・アシスト・ドライビング」に変更することを提案したと明らかにした。同システムは運転を支援するものではあるが、完全な自動運転ではない。

フルセルフドライビングはすでにオランダやベルギーなど欧州の一部で認可されている。

しかし、スウェーデンやフランスを含むいくつかのＥＵ加盟国は、同システムが制限速度を超えることへの懸念を表明しており、１０月に予定されていたＥＵの採決は、一部の国が追加試験を行う間、少なくとも１２月まで延期された。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：減速するテスラ、頼みの綱は国内ライバル勢の出遅れ 焦点：テスラ、ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」で試す規制の限界 アングル：ロボタクシー拡大に慎重になったテスラ　投資家の不満解消できるか アングル：テスラのロボタクシー、導入済みテキサス3都市では課題山積 アングル：テスラの納車台数、26年予想下振れ　3年連続減少の見方も 最終更新: 10/7(水) 19:43 ロイター

item.title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 slip from record highs as yields and oil rebound
item.description: The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 eased from record highs on Wednesday as Treasury yields and oil prices rebounded, keeping investors cautious as they awaited the minutes of the Federal Reserve's September meeting.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 eased from record highs on Wednesday as Treasury yields and oil prices rebounded, keeping investors cautious as they awaited the minutes of the Federal Reserve's September meeting. Sentiment turned more cautious as investors reassessed the outlook for interest rates and energy costs. Brent crude was back above the psychologically important $100-a-barrel level as Middle East supply concerns persisted. "We're seeing a little bit of profit-taking today. The market is very focused on the Fed minutes, but ultimately it's where oil prices and yields move that will determine the market's direction today," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities. Chip stocks were among the top decliners. Memory chip firm Micron Technology (MU.O) dropped 2.3%, chip giant Nvidia (NVDA.O) eased 0.7% and the broader Philadelphia chip index (.SOX) fell 2.3%. Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) lost 1.7% after a Financial Times report that [USN:L6N45S1CR TEXT:"the rockets-to-AI firm"] was seeking $40 billion in financing to fund purchases of Nvidia chips. Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sectors traded lower, with the materials (.SPLRCM) and industrials (.SPLRCI) leading losses. Energy (.SPNY) and healthcare (.SPXHC) were higher, up 0.6% each. At 9:43 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 472.21 points, or 0.92%, to 51,049.07, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 44.80 points, or 0.56%, to 7,775.04 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 235.16 points, or 0.85%, to 27,364.73. The yield on 30-year Treasury bonds rose to the highest since 2002, last at 5.72% ahead of the release later in the day of [USN:L6N45S0TH TEXT:"minutes from the US Federal Reserve's"] September policy meeting, when policymakers raised interest rates to combat inflation. Traders widely expect the Fed to hold rates steady at its October meeting, but a December hike remains on the cards, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. The S&P 500's equal-weighted counterpart (.SPXEW) , meanwhile, stands more than 5% away from record highs and the interest-rate-sensitive Russell 2000 small-cap index (.RUT) is down more than 8% from its all-time high. MARKETS BRACE FOR EARNINGS Focus will likely shift to how corporate America is faring as the third-quarter earnings season kicks off next week, with a number of high-profile financial firms expected to report on Tuesday. US stocks have been buoyed lately by optimism around the AI trade and expectations of strong corporate earnings, despite higher energy prices and a summer selloff in bond markets that fueled concerns about tighter monetary policy. Analysts currently expect S&P 500 earnings growth of 30.6%, in aggregate, for the July-to-September period, led by an expected 114.7% jump in energy earnings, followed by a 66.5% estimated surge in tech results, according to LSEG. While the 30% profit growth is smaller than in the second quarter, when S&P 500 companies posted a 54% jump in earnings, investors expect a largely positive season to underpin record-high stock markets. Among other movers, Roblox fell 1.6% after Google and Unity announced a partnership on a new AI gaming platform that could compete with the [USN:L4N45T0W0 TEXT:"gaming platform's"] offerings. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.74-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 3.19-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 8 new 52-week highs and 5 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 8 new highs and 129 new lows.

item.title: Morning Bid: Storm brewing
item.description: As the US third-quarter earnings season gets set to kick off, Wall Street's S&P 500 joined the Nasdaq in setting a new record high on Tuesday - its first in about six weeks.
item.dc:creator: Mike Dolan
item.content:encoded: As the US third-quarter earnings season gets set to kick off, Wall Street's S&P 500 joined the Nasdaq in [USN:L6N45S0IV TEXT:"setting a new record high"] on Tuesday - its first in about six weeks. Consensus forecasts are for another AI-led blockbuster rise in profits in the July-September period, with LSEG data showing expectations of an overall 30% annual expansion. With Treasury yields still hovering [USN:L4N45T003 TEXT:"close to 24-year highs"], bond markets are navigating another heavy week of US debt sales. Tuesday's auction of 3-year notes appeared to go relatively smoothly, unlike last month's jarring 5-year sale, but the rates taken up were still their highest in 20 years. Sales of 10-year and 30-year paper will follow today and tomorrow, respectively. Even though the rise in Federal Reserve interest rate expectations has largely been responsible for the surge in Treasury yields over recent months, the risk premium that accounts for investor uncertainty about holding long-term debt to maturity is also back on the rise. The New York Fed's estimate of the 10-year Treasury "term premium", which feeds off long-term debt and inflation concerns, has climbed to its highest in 12 years this week at 96 basis points. Helping gauge the next steps from the Fed, the central bank will release minutes of its September meeting on Wednesday - a readout on what was said to be a [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"unanimous decision"] to lift rates for the first time in three years. In the background, the Atlanta Fed's real-time GDPNow model eased a bit to 3.7% from as high as 5.1% previously - although this may be partly related to mechanical GDP impact from a [USN:L1N45R0RR TEXT:"rising trade deficit"] in August. That, though, was in turn driven largely by a jump in imports that speaks as much to stepped-up activity and the AI boom. In Europe, French and other euro zone government debt markets [USN:L6N45S0DI TEXT:"calmed somewhat"] on Tuesday, with one eye on the [USN:L8N45R1J6 TEXT:"spending cut plans"] of far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who's now the favorite to win the April election. Chart of the day French government debt risk premia versus Germany surged last month to the widest in 15 years, as the country struggles again to pass an [USN:L1N45N09R TEXT:"annual budget"] that would keep a lid on its annual deficit of more than 5% of GDP as debt piles soar. The widening of French debt spreads and rising nominal borrowing costs have sent a jolt through all [USN:L8N45S0RJ TEXT:"euro zone government debt markets"], given the outside chance it seeds a repeat of the existential euro debt crisis of 2010-2012. Belgian, Italian and Greek debt markets felt most of the spillover last month. Today's events to watch US 10-year note auction (1 p.m. EDT) Fed publishes September policy meeting minutes (2 p.m. EDT) Before you go, listen to the latest episode of the Morning Bid daily podcast, where we discuss the S&P 500's fresh record and more. item.title: ルビオ米国務長官、ギリシャと安全保障上の脅威に共同対処と表明
item.description: [アテネ ７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[アテネ ７日 ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は７日、米国と「北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の強力かつ模範的な同盟国」であるギリシャが法執行機関間で新たなテロ対策情報の共有を開始すると表明した。

アテネを公式訪問中のルビオ氏は、ギリシャは特に大規模な移民や人身売買による脅威にさらされていると述べた。

ギリシャのゲラペトリティス外相と並んで記者団に対し、「両国に共通するこれらの脅威と闘う取り組みの一環として、それぞれの法執行機関間のテロ対策情報共有を強化する共同安全保障プログラムを確立する新たな覚書を締結したことを、誇りを持って発表する」と語った。

ゲラペトリティス氏は、ホルムズ海峡で実行可能な和平プロセスが進めば、ギリシャは米国と協力し、同海峡での海上支援を提供する用意があると述べた。

ギルフォイル駐ギリシャ米大使が「米国は影響力を行使してギリシャ政府を弱体化させることができる」と脅したとの疑惑について米上院議員らが懸念を表明したことを巡っては、ルビオ氏は同大使を擁護。「ここにあるわれわれの大使館は素晴らしい仕事をしている。われわれの大使はこの地で力強い大使としての役割を果たしている」と述べた。

item.title: TSX falls as rising yields pressure financials, miners
item.description: Canada's benchmark stock index slipped to near one-week low on Wednesday, with miners and financials leading losses, as elevated oil prices and climbing yields stoked inflationary fears and soured risk appetite.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Anand R
item.content:encoded: Canada's benchmark stock index slipped to near one-week low on Wednesday, with miners and financials leading losses, as elevated oil prices and climbing yields stoked inflationary fears and soured risk appetite. The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) fell 1.33% to 35,174.22 points at 10:08 a.m. ET (1408 GMT), touching its lowest since October 1. Gold fell 1.6% to a two-month low, pressured by a strong US dollar and Treasury yields Materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , which includes precious metal miners, declined 2.7% to its lowest level in two months Brent crude prices rose 1.1% to $101.68 a barrel, reinforcing expectations of higher interest rates "Of late, bond yields have been the big driver of performance of our (Canadian) market," said Matthew Kempton, portfolio manager at Verecan Capital Management "When interest rates move higher, it can be quite poor for [financials'] core business, especially with the yield curve becoming flatter and spreads getting smaller," Kempton said The heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) slipped 1.7%; Royal Bank of Canada (RY.TO) and Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD.TO) fell more than 1.7% each Yields on the US benchmark 10-year Treasury note and 30-year Treasury note climbed to their highest levels since 2002 at 5.3177% and 5.6971%, respectively The yield on the Canadian 10-year government bond also inched higher Markets will now eye minutes from the US Federal Reserve's September meeting later on Wednesday for clues on the monetary policy path Traders expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged at its October meeting and an 86% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in December, according to data compiled by LSEG In Canada, investors are pricing in at least one 25-basis-point hike by the central bank by year-end

item.title: 独ポルシェ、販売減前提に事業再構築 最高価格帯に注力
item.description:
Rachel More Ilona Wissenbach
[ベルリン／フランクフルト ７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独ポルシェ、販売減前提に事業再構築　最高価格帯に注力 19:11 配信

写真はポルシェのロゴ。3月10日、ドイツ・ケルンで撮影。REUTERS/Jana Rodenbusch

Rachel More　Ilona Wissenbach

[ベルリン／フランクフルト ７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級スポーツカーメーカー、ポルシェは７日、販売台数の減少を前提に事業を再構築すると明らかにした。需要が低迷する中でも、高級モデルへの注力で利益率の回復を目指す。

再建計画では、将来の損益分岐点となる販売台数を２０万台未満に引き下げる方針を示した。昨年の総納車台数２７万９４４９台を大幅に下回る水準となる。

ポルシェの世界納車台数は上場を果たした２０２２年から既に１０％近く減少した。中国での需要急減と米国の関税が打撃となっている。

南西部バイザッハの開発センターで開いた投資家向け説明会で、ミヒャエル・ライタース最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「９１１」などの高級スポーツカーに注力することで経営を立て直せると訴えた。年間販売の最高価格帯にある１万台について、販売価格の引き上げを目指す。

「世界で最も魅力的なスポーツカーメーカーとしてのポルシェの地位を強化したい」と述べ、ブランド価値の面でフェラーリやルイ・ヴィトンと肩を並べる存在に位置付けた。

＜２桁の利益率回復へ険しい道のり＞

ライタース氏は当面コスト削減に重点を置くと説明した。

ポルシェは今回の戦略で、グループ営業利益率の長期目標を１５％に設定した。おおむね５年以内を指す中期では、１０─１５％を目指す。利益率は上場した４年前の１０％台後半から、２５年には１．１％に急低下した。

発表を受けて株価は３．２％上昇した。

ライタース氏によると、現状では中期目標の下限を達成する見通しだ。それ以上の改善には、一段と踏み込んだ事業再編か「より好ましい事業環境」が必要になるという。

同氏は既存の人員削減策や管理職を４０％減らす計画に加え、開発費と販売費の削減で経営基盤を強化すると述べた。コスト削減に向け、同じフォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）傘下の高級車メーカー、アウディとの車台共用も拡大する方針だ。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：空前のＡＩ投資、相応の経済効果実現へなお高いハードル コラム：円急伸で揺らぐキャリートレード、見つからない次の調達通貨 アングル：世界市場が当面向き合う6つのリスク、地政学や金融政策・ＡＩなど アングル：湾岸諸国、インフラ整備に重点投資　ホルムズ海峡封鎖で紛争耐性強化へ アングル：東京から欧州まで、猛暑で広がる男性の「短パン通勤」 最終更新: 10/7(水) 19:11 ロイター

item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 7 : Microsoft will unveil on Wednesday a new laptop powered by Nvidia's chips, seeking to turn Windows into a platform for AI agents to handle tasks such as writing code without having to access the cloud, analysts said.For Microsoft, the move represents a bet that some work that currently

item.content:encoded:

Microsoft, Nvidia CEOs to unveil new AI laptop at San Francisco event

FILE PHOTO: Executive Chairman and CEO of Microsoft Corporation Satya Nadella speaks during the "Microsoft Build: AI Day" event in Jakarta, Indonesia, April 30, 2024. REUTERS/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana/ File Photo

FAST

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 7 : Microsoft will unveil on Wednesday a new laptop powered by Nvidia's chips, seeking to turn Windows into a platform for AI agents to handle tasks such as writing code without having to access the cloud, analysts said. For Microsoft, the move represents a bet that some work that currently takes place in its costly Azure cloud computing data centers can be shifted to high-powered Windows machines in businesses and homes, a market where the Redmond, Washington-based firm retains a stronghold — and where its customers foot the hardware bills. It is a market opportunity that longtime rival Apple is also chasing with new Mac computers. For Nvidia, cracking the Windows PC market could help it go after one of the last major markets dominated by its longtime rivals Intel and Advanced Micro Devices. The Microsoft-hosted event in San Francisco, which the company billed as an update on its Windows operating system and Surface line of hardware, will be the culmination of years of work between the flagship operating system maker for PCs and the AI chip company to bring many tasks such as writing computer code or tackling complex business projects directly to desktops and laptops with Nvidia's RTX Spark chips announced in June.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will take the stage to introduce the Surface Laptop Ultra, as the new machine will be called. One of the key challenges for Microsoft and Nvidia will be to show that agents, the long-running AI systems that can tackle complex problems on their own, can be safely contained on personal computers. Nvidia is already trying to prevent a repeat of the hack of AI hub Hugging Face, while Apple is looking to tighten up the process for giving AI agents full access to a Mac computer's hard drive. But analysts said the biggest question will be the price of the new offerings after a memory-chip crunch has driven up prices for desktop and laptop machines. When Microsoft originally pitched the idea of running AI tasks on PCs two years ago to save on costs, the laptops were mostly priced below $2,000, but in recent weeks, Nvidia increased the price of an AI desktop machine called the DGX Spark by about 75 per cent to $6,950, thanks to the surging costs of its 128 gigabytes of memory. Anshel Sag, an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, told Reuters that the memory prices are affecting both Apple and Microsoft's efforts. Two years ago, "the software wasn't ready, but the hardware was. Now the software is ready and the hardware is too expensive to actually run it locally," Sag said. "So it's becoming this thing where only the people who have the budget can really afford to run AI locally."
